text.p: British drug discovery group Chiroscience Group Plc said on Tuesday it had formed an alliance with Powderject Pharmaceuticals for the development of local anaesthetic products delivered in Powderject's proprietary needleless, painfree, drug-injector technology.
The alliance will focus on the development of both lignocaine and levobupivacaine products.
A growing number of surgical procedures, more than 40 million each year, are being conducted under local anaesthesia because of advantages both in cost and in using minimally invasive surgery.

The market for pain management is expected to grow to $7 billion by 2005 and the potential markets for widespread use of needleless surgical and dental products are in excess of $300 million, Chiroscience said in a statement.

The products will be developed jointly with Powderject responsible for device and formulation development and Chiroscience managing and directing the clinical trials programme. They intend to share equally the rewards from the products.
Powderject is expected to seek a listing on the London Stock Market later this year, to raise 30-35 million stg and have a market capitalisation of around 100 million stg.
